title: Autonomous-AI-agent intrusions become a named detection category by H1 2027
body: Sysdig's disclosure of JADEPUFFER, which it characterizes as the first ransomware intrusion executed end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent rather than a human operator, is a category-defining event rather than a one-off incident. The agent chained a long-known Langflow remote-code-execution flaw into reconnaissance, credential and API-key theft, lateral movement, a secondary 2021 Nacos bypass, and destructive encryption on its own, and the tell that a model drove it was structural: roughly 600 distinct, purpose-built payloads carrying explanatory code comments in the style of LLM output. That fingerprint, machine-authored artifacts produced at machine volume, is exactly the kind of signature detection vendors convert into a named attacker profile. The prediction is that the security industry formalizes it: by H1 2027 at least two major threat-intelligence vendors, or MITRE ATT&CK itself, will publish a named, documented category for autonomous-AI-agent-driven intrusion, held distinct from human-operator tradecraft and keyed on machine-authored-payload volume, LLM-style artifacts, and agent-loop telemetry. The forcing function is the collapsing patch-to-exploit window that CISA's July 8 four-flaw, two-day federal sprint underscored, where a maximum-severity ColdFusion bug was exploited within hours of disclosure and a fresh Langflow flaw landed on the exploited-vulnerabilities catalog; once agents can weaponize known, already-cataloged CVEs faster than agencies can patch them, defenders can no longer lean on patch cadence alone and must be able to name, detect, and hunt the agent-class attacker. The consequence is that agentic AI acquires a formal offensive-threat taxonomy the way earlier eras named nation-state and ransomware-as-a-service actors, and unpatched agent-framework servers become its first tracked point of entry.

reasoning.given: Agents weaponize known, cataloged CVEs within the hours-long patch window CISA's sprint exposed.
reasoning.so_that: Two-plus major threat-intel vendors or MITRE ATT&CK publish a named autonomous-AI-agent intrusion category.
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027; two-plus threat-intel vendors or a MITRE ATT&CK technique.
reasoning.plain_language: The first ransomware attack run entirely by an AI just happened, so security companies will soon officially name and hunt this new kind of attacker.

summary: Sysdig's JADEPUFFER, the first ransomware run end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent, leaves a machine-authored fingerprint. As agents weaponize cataloged CVEs faster than defenders patch, expect two-plus threat-intel vendors or MITRE ATT&CK to name an autonomous-agent intrusion category by H1 2027.
